chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Awrama and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Jadalī entered upon Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and he عليه السلام said: O Abū ʿAbdillāh, shall I not inform you of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have better than it, and they shall be secure from terror on that Day. And whoever brings an evil deed, their faces shall be cast into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?

He said: Yes, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, may I be your ransom. He said: The good deed is recognition of the wilayah and love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt; and the evil deed is denial of the wilayah and hatred for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.
Then he recited this verse to him.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the People of the Household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.السَّيِّئَةُ: the evil deed, interpreted here as denial of the wilayah and hatred of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الْحَسَنَةُ: the good deed, interpreted here as recognition of the wilayah and love of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةِ: the divinely ordained authority and guardianship associated with the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.بُغْضُنَا: hatred toward us, meaning enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.حُبُّنَا: love for us, meaning devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: How do the Imams عليهم السلام interpret the Quranic verse about bringing a good deed or an evil deed?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an interpretation of the Quranic contrast between the good deed and the evil deed in relation to wilayah. It explains that recognizing the wilayah and loving the Ahl al-Bayt is the good deed that brings security, while denying the wilayah and hating the Ahl al-Bayt is the evil deed that brings punishment. The narration highlights the central theological significance of allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt in understanding Quranic reward and punishment.
